To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dust masses implied by the star formation history are consistent with those inferred from the observed submillimetre luminosity function, (ii) the dust masses in the submillimetre population are comparable to the dust masses in local spheroidal systems, (iii) the dust masses of the submillimmetre population can be reproduced by a simple model of dust evolution in spheroidal galaxies.
the star formation history implies the existence of a large amount of dust in the early Universe, and that a large fraction of the missing metals is associated with this dust.

the star formation history at high redshift is consistent with the observed distribution of metals in the Universe, and the observed dust mass in submillimetre galaxies is consistent with the star formation history, the observed metal distribution and a simple model for dust in spheroidal galaxies.
